overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body responsible for the Medford Public Schools, overseeing operating budgets, district policies, collective bargaining, curriculum frameworks, and school capital infrastructure. The archive covers 132 meetings across three terms from May 2022 through October 2026. Over this span, the committee navigated leadership transitions including the retirement of Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent and the appointment of Dr. Suzanne Galusi as interim and subsequently permanent superintendent. Its work has encompassed major infrastructure projects—notably a new comprehensive high school building initiative through the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) and district-wide HVAC upgrades—alongside recurring operational hurdles in school transportation, elementary overcrowding, and after-school capacity. As of October 2026, the committee is advancing geothermal and accelerated repair facility projects, expanding after-school services, and developing a community-informed district strategic plan.

threads.name: Medford High School building project
threads.summary: Following consultant recommendations and district reviews, the committee voted in April 2023 to submit a Statement of Interest to the MSBA Core Program for Medford High School [M23#6]. The district entered the eligibility period in late 2023, after which the committee established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee's governance structure, project goals, and appointments [M42#5, M47#5, M52#8]. In 2025, Left Field was selected as Owner's Project Manager, and the committee executed a feasibility study agreement for a certified capacity of 1,395 students [M83#7, M91#5]. Educational plans, Chapter 74 vocational viability, and design alternatives were evaluated and revised through 2026, including adjustments to navigate a 1967 DCR deed restriction affecting Edgerly Field [M108#3, M120#2, M126#1, M127#7].

threads.name: District facilities and HVAC capital projects
threads.summary: Widespread cooling failures and aging equipment prompted severe operational challenges, leading the committee in April 2024 to approve a fossil-fuel equipment restriction policy and adopt a $15 to $20 million decarbonization scope for the McGlynn and Andrews middle schools [M34#6, M54#6, M54#13]. A comprehensive facilities assessment identified $83.7 million in needed repairs across five schools, spurring bond authorizations of over $25.7 million and Accelerated Repair submissions to the MSBA [M79#6, M86#1, M88#7, M102#3]. By late 2026, the committee approved a $22.7 million schematic design and Construction Manager at Risk procurement for Roberts Elementary, while selecting a ground-source geothermal heat pump system for Missituck Elementary [M128#4, M132#4, M132#5].

threads.name: District operating budget and fiscal planning
threads.summary: The committee enacted annual operating budgets amid fiscal challenges, including an early multi-million-dollar gap in FY23 and a projected $2.5 million shortfall during FY24 that required expenditure remediation [M03#5, M04#6, M46#4, M49#5]. In 2024, the committee approved a formal budget schedule policy, successfully requested a level-service FY25 budget, and allocated voter-approved override funds to restore positions and finance reserves [M56#9, M58#9, M80#7]. Budget reviews continued into FY27, balancing gap closures, revenue projections, and stabilization reserves through joint meetings with the City Council and quarterly financial reporting [M113#3, M125#4, M132#6].

threads.name: Superintendent leadership and evaluation
threads.summary: Throughout 2022 and 2023, the committee evaluated Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent using customized indicators and DESE templates, rating her overall performance as proficient [M02#9, M28#4, M31#2]. Following executive session contract negotiations across 2024, Dr. Edouard-Vincent departed the district in January 2025, and Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi was appointed Interim Superintendent [M62#2, M78#2, M80#5]. After completing self-evaluations and entry findings, the committee voted in February 2026 to appoint Dr. Galusi as permanent superintendent and later executed a three-year employment contract [M107#6, M108#4, M118#6].

threads.name: Collective bargaining and labor relations
threads.summary: The committee managed complex labor relations, including an impasse and state mediation with the Medford Teachers Association (MTA) before reaching a four-year contract agreement in December 2022 [M05#5, M09#4, M15#5]. Over subsequent years, agreements were ratified with non-instructional units including secretaries, custodians, administrators, cafeteria workers, and nurses [M06#1, M36#1, M60#2, M93#6, M99#1]. In April 2025, the committee ratified a successor three-year contract with the MTA adding instructional time, while continuing to negotiate grievance and compensation updates across multiple bargaining units into 2026 [M90#3, M97#2, M111#1, M129#1].

threads.name: Student transportation and safety
threads.summary: Transportation operations faced consistent strain from vendor bus driver shortages, leading to overcrowded routes, bus stop consolidation, and eligibility changes [M05#3, M65#12, M71#4]. In response, the committee approved a new five-year contract with Eastern Bus, directed bus safety reports, deployed paraprofessionals as rotating bus monitors, and requested municipal enforcement of bus stop-arm cameras [M95#4, M98#8, M101#6]. Student representatives highlighted boarding congestion and transit timing, resulting in an audit by Safe Routes to School and the eventual rollout of a high school late bus [M50#4, M103#3, M131#4].

threads.name: Elementary enrollment and space utilization
threads.summary: Enrollment imbalances created severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary School, leading staff and committee members to call for redistricting and space reviews [M65#8, M66#6, M89#4]. In June 2025, the committee relocated Medford Early Education Program (MEEP) classrooms to Missituk Elementary and formed a strategic space planning task force [M94#6, M94#7]. While consultant recommendations explored reconfiguring grade spans to K-4 and 5-8 middle schools, the committee voted in July 2026 to delay structural middle school reconfigurations until at least 2028 and held an elementary reassignment policy for revision [M103#5, M127#4, M131#5].

threads.name: Before and after-school programming expansion
threads.summary: Long student waitlists and staffing constraints plagued before and after-school childcare programs across multiple terms, leading the committee to replace waitlists with lotteries and revise sliding-scale rate cards [M14#4, M21#5, M23#8]. In May 2025, the committee partnered with the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) to restructure and expand program capacity [M92#2]. By 2026, the committee approved rate adjustments, full-time site coordinators, and a restructured leadership model, ultimately achieving a 50 percent increase in enrollment and a 68 percent reduction in waitlists [M97#3, M118#4, M129#5, M132#3].
